_comment: Release dates verified against the package registries: npm (registry.npmjs.org time field) for the front-end tools, Maven Central directory listings for the JVM tools, services.gradle.org for Gradle, postgresql.org announcements for PostgreSQL server. Support windows follow each project's published policy; Angular = 6 months active + 12 months LTS; Spring Boot = ~13 months of OSS support per minor (eol here = OSS end — commercial support runs longer); PostgreSQL = five years per major. Regenerate the 'current' fields when bumping: npm view <pkg> version / the registry metadata.

angular.name: Angular
angular.cadence: Two majors a year, roughly May and November.
angular.policy: 6 months active support, then 12 months long-term support. An Angular major is out of support 18 months after release.

releases.headline: Signal Forms, the Resource API and @angular/aria go stable. OnPush becomes the default change detection strategy. HttpClient uses fetch by default. New @Service() decorator.
Vitest becomes the default test runner via the stable @angular/build:unit-test builder; Karma is deprecated.
Signals stabilise (effect, linkedSignal, toSignal). Zoneless change detection reaches developer preview maturity. Vitest support lands experimentally.
standalone: true becomes the default — no more standalone flag on new components. linkedSignal and resource() arrive in preview.
Zoneless change detection in experimental preview. Built-in control flow and deferrable views go stable. Material 3 support.
The rebrand and angular.dev. Built-in control flow (@if/@for/@switch) and @defer arrive. esbuild/Vite application builder becomes the default.
Signals land in developer preview. takeUntilDestroyed and DestroyRef. Required inputs. Standalone ng new schematic.
Standalone APIs go stable. Functional router guards, directive composition API. Legacy compiler compatibility removed.
Standalone components in developer preview — the beginning of the end for NgModules. Typed reactive forms. inject() becomes broadly usable.

rxjs.name: RxJS
rxjs._currentMajorNote: Points at the 7.8 line rather than 7, so the dashboard dates the release line the current version belongs to (Dec 2022) instead of v7.0.0's date (Apr 2021).
rxjs.cadence: Irregular. RxJS 7 has been the stable line since 2021.
rxjs.policy: No formal LTS window. RxJS 8 is on hold pending the TC39/WHATWG Observable standard, so 7.8 is the production answer.

releases.headline: On hold by design: the maintainers are waiting for Observable to be standardised on the web platform so RxJS 8 can align with it rather than diverge. Do not plan around a date.
The current stable line. 7.8.2 is the latest patch.
firstValueFrom/lastValueFrom replace the deprecated toPromise(). retry() takes a config object. Much smaller bundles and better TypeScript inference.
The pipeable-operator break: .pipe(map(x => x)) replaced patched prototype methods (obs.map(...)). Everything since is a refinement of this model.
The patched-prototype era you will still meet in old codebases: import 'rxjs/add/operator/map' and obs.map(...).

vitest.name: Vitest
vitest.policy: No formal LTS. The Angular CLI pins a compatible range through @angular/build.

releases.headline: Browser Mode leaves experimental; providers move to separate @vitest/browser-* packages. poolMatchGlobs/environmentMatchGlobs and deps.inline/deps.external removed in favour of projects and server.deps.*.
The workspace config is deprecated in 3.2 in favour of the projects option in the root config. Annotation API added.
Reporter and snapshot overhaul.
First stable major, Vite 5 alignment.

pnpm.name: pnpm
pnpm.cadence: Roughly a major a year, in the first half of the year.
pnpm.policy: No formal LTS. Pin it with the packageManager field in package.json.

releases.headline: The big config break: settings no longer read from the pnpm field in package.json or from non-auth .npmrc — they move to pnpm-workspace.yaml and ~/.config/pnpm/config.yaml. npm_config_* becomes pnpm_config_*. pnpm is pure ESM, the store is a single SQLite database, supply-chain defaults are on (minimumReleaseAge, blockExoticSubdeps), and Node 22+ is required. allowBuilds replaces the onlyBuiltDependencies family.

Dependency lifecycle scripts no longer run on install — a direct response to the Rspack supply-chain attack. Opt packages in with pnpm.onlyBuiltDependencies. Peer-dependency hashes in the lockfile move from MD5 to SHA256.
Lockfile format v9.
Lockfile format v6.

typescript.name: TypeScript
typescript.policy: Angular pins a supported TypeScript range per major — check the compatibility table before upgrading either one.

kotlin.name: Kotlin
kotlin.cadence: Two feature releases a year (x.y.0, roughly June and December), with x.y.20-style tooling updates between.
kotlin.policy: No LTS — fixes land in the newest line. Mind which version your build actually uses: Spring Boot's BOM pins its own Kotlin (2.3.21 on Boot 4.1) unless you override it.

releases.headline: Context parameters and explicit backing fields go stable; rich errors and collection literals arrive experimentally. JVM target 26.
Unused-return-value checker, nested type aliases stable, Java 25 support. The line Spring Boot 4.1 pins (2.3.21).
Guard conditions, non-local break/continue and multi-dollar interpolation go stable; context parameters arrive in preview. Interface methods compile to JVM default methods.
Preview syntax: guard conditions in when, non-local break/continue, $$-interpolation. JSpecify nullability violations become errors by default.
K2: the rewritten compiler frontend goes stable and becomes the default — JetBrains measured up to ~94% faster clean builds. The 1.x → 2.x line every migration story starts from.
The last pre-K2 line — what legacy Kotlin means in 2026: no K2, kapt-era tooling.

spring.name: Spring Boot
spring.cadence: A minor every six months (May/June and November); each minor gets ~13 months of open-source patches.
spring.policy: OSS support per minor is ~13 months, then commercial-only (eol below = OSS end). 3.5 was the final 3.x line and left OSS support in June 2026. The Boot BOM decides your library versions — on 4.1: Framework 7.0.8, Security 7.1.0, Jackson 3.1.4, jOOQ 3.21.5, Kotlin 2.3.21.

releases.headline: Framework 7.0.8, Security 7.1. OpenTelemetry reads the standard OTel environment variables; process details in the info endpoint; Jackson 3.1. Runs on Java 17–26.

The big one: Framework 7, Jackson 3 by default, JSpecify null-safety, API versioning, modular starters (spring-boot-starter-web → -webmvc), RestTestClient, Testcontainers 2, JUnit 6. Undertow support removed.
The final 3.x line — out of OSS support since 2026-06-30 (commercial support continues into 2032). If you are here, the upgrade target is 4.x.
MockMvcTester (AssertJ), structured logging (ecs/logstash/gelf), @MockitoBean replaces @MockBean.
RestClient arrives; virtual threads via spring.threads.virtual.enabled (Java 21).
The jakarta.* break: Jakarta EE 9, Framework 6, Java 17 baseline, Micrometer Observation API.

gradle.name: Gradle
gradle.cadence: A major roughly every two years; minors every six-to-eight weeks. Pinned per project by the wrapper.
gradle.policy: No LTS — only the current major line gets fixes. The wrapper makes upgrades per-repository: ./gradlew wrapper --gradle-version <v>.

releases.headline: Requires Java 17 to run; build scripts use Kotlin 2.2 (DSL) and Groovy 4; the configuration cache becomes the preferred — not yet default — execution mode (that flip is slated for Gradle 10). 9.1 adds Java 25.
The line that set today's idioms: configuration cache stable (8.1), Kotlin DSL the default for new builds (8.2), full Java 21 (8.5).
Version catalogs (libs.versions.toml) arrive, stable in 7.4.

postgres.name: PostgreSQL
postgres.cadence: A major every September; quarterly minors (Feb/May/Aug/Nov).
postgres.policy: Five years of fixes per major, then EOL — the final minor lands in the November five years after release. No LTS tiers: every supported major gets the same treatment.

releases.headline: SQL/PGQ property-graph queries, ON CONFLICT DO SELECT, REPACK (online table rebuild), parallel autovacuum. GA expected in the usual September–October window.
Asynchronous I/O (io_uring), uuidv7(), virtual generated columns, B-tree skip scan, temporal PK/FK constraints, OAuth authentication, RETURNING OLD/NEW.
JSON_TABLE, incremental backup (pg_basebackup + pg_combinebackup), vacuum memory use cut up to 20×, logical-replication slots survive failover and pg_upgrade.
pg_stat_io, parallel FULL hash joins, logical replication from standbys, SQL/JSON constructors.
MERGE arrives. zstd compression, server-side backup compression, 25–400% faster sorts.
The oldest line still in support — and only until this November. Plan the upgrade.

jooq.name: jOOQ
jooq.cadence: A minor roughly yearly; patch releases continuously across the last few minors.
jooq.policy: The open-source edition is Apache-2.0 and licensed for use with open-source databases only (PostgreSQL qualifies) — commercial databases need a paid edition. OSS edition requires JDK 21 since 3.20. Spring Boot 4.1 manages 3.21.5.

releases.headline: Redacted columns, UDT improvements, more enterprise dialects. The line Boot 4.1 manages.
JDK 21 baseline for the OSS edition; formal Kotlin 2 and Scala 3 support; reactor extensions.
Implicit to-many path joins — the natural partner of MULTISET — and the official jooq-codegen-gradle plugin.
Expanded SQL/JSON support and query diagnostics/linting.
Kotlin coroutine support (jooq-kotlin-coroutines), reactive transactions, Java 17 baseline.
Public query object model (QOM) API.
The headline release: MULTISET nested collections and R2DBC support — type-safe nested DTOs straight from SQL, no ORM.

jackson.name: Jackson
jackson.cadence: Minors roughly quarterly on the 3.x line; the 2.x line continues in maintenance in parallel (currently 2.22).
jackson.policy: Jackson 3 (tools.jackson.*) is where new work happens — Spring Boot 4 defaults to it (managing 3.1.x) while still managing a Jackson 2 BOM for migration. Framework 7 plans to drop Jackson 2 auto-detection in 7.1 and support in 7.2.

releases.headline: Current 3.x release branch.
First 3.x LTS branch — what Spring Boot 4.1 manages (3.1.4).

The 2→3 break: Java packages and Maven groups move com.fasterxml.jackson.* → tools.jackson.* (annotations stay put, so 2 and 3 coexist), ObjectMapper becomes immutable behind JsonMapper.builder(), JacksonException goes unchecked, defaults get saner (unknown properties no longer fail, dates serialise as ISO strings). Java 17 baseline.
Current 2.x maintenance branch — fine while dependencies catch up; the package rename means 2 and 3 can share a classpath.
2.x LTS branch — what Boot 4.1's Jackson 2 BOM manages (2.21.4).
